full_judgment: 11. Admittedly the land in suit of the schedules were recorded in the name of Baisnab in CS (Khasra) Khatian No. 267 (Exhibit 2A) and CS . (Khasra) Khatian No. 260. The plaintiffs have led evidence to show that the, suit land so recorded belonged to Baisnab Chandra Dey who has acquired raiyat right taking lease from the landlord Ram Krishna Chowdhury and others and the tenancy in (Nal land) Exhibit 2 has been taken lease by Baisnab from Khas Mahal, Patiya at a rental of Rs 1/4 and the Empress of India the rent free tenancy in schedule recorded in Exhibit 2(a) (Bhiti land) in raiyati right was taken lease of by Baisnab from one Ram Krishna Charan and others. The presumption of the CS Khatian under section 103(B) of the Bengal Tenancy Act is that every entry in a record of rights finally published shall be the evidence of the matter referred to in such entry and shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved to be incorrect. Reference may be made in this regard to the case of Akrab Ali and others vs Zahiruddin Kari and others. 30 DLR (SC) 81.
